Position description The School of Information at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for appointment to the faculty at the Assistant Professor rank. Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is a field of expertise focused on the evolving relationship between people and computing systems. HCI researchers design and study new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with technology, and investigate how emerging computing systems shape human capabilities, practices, organizations, and society. Methods include the design and development of novel systems, experimentation, qualitative and ethnographic research, participatory design, computational methods, field studies, and mixed-methods research. We seek applicants who are defining the next generation of human-computer interaction: developing new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with increasingly intelligent computing systems. We are particularly interested in scholars who both imagine and build new forms of human-computer interaction and rigorously investigate how these technologies shape people, organizations, and society. We welcome research across HCI and related fields, including, but not limited to, human-AI interaction and collaboration, intelligent and adaptive interfaces, social and collaborative computing, the future of work, accessibility, values such as sustainability, privacy, and justice in and through design, ubiquitous and embodied computing, information visualization, human-robot interaction, and emerging interaction modalities. We welcome a broad range of methodological approaches, including the design and development of novel systems, experimental and computational methods, qualitative and ethnographic research, field studies, participatory and critical design methods, and mixed-methods approaches. Successful candidates will demonstrate the potential to establish an internationally recognized research program, contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in HCI, and engage with the School of Information’s interdisciplinary community. The School of Information is a graduate research and education community committed to expanding access to information and to improving its usability, reliability, and credibility while preserving security and privacy. This requires the insights of scholars from diverse fields — information and computer science, design, social sciences, management, law, and policy. We are committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual-career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non- traditional career paths or who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit New Senate Faculty | Office for Faculty Equity & Welfare. job_4c77c25a4b4b8cff: Explore Academic Positions at Harvard Open Postdoc Position – Rowland Institute Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Position Details Title Open Postdoc Position – Rowland Institute School Faculty of Arts and Sciences Department/Area Optical microscopy Position Description The brain computes through distributed neural circuits on millisecond timescales. To understand how the brain operates, the Z. Wang Lab at the Rowland Institute at Harvard develops optical tools to record and control neural activity across the entire brain at cellular and millisecond resolution. By combining advanced microscopy, genetically encoded voltage indicators, two-photon optogenetics, and zebrafish neuroscience, we aim to enable causal interrogation of brain-wide neural dynamics at single-cell and single-spike resolution. The system will combine a high-speed light-sheet microscope, a two-photon holographic stimulation system, and software for instrument control, synchronization, and image acquisition. This project builds on our recent paper (Nature Methods 2026, in press, preprint) on voltage imaging of neurons distributed across the larval zebrafish brain at over 200 Hz. The postdoctoral fellow will play a leading role in designing, building, integrating, and validating the next-generation platform.More information is available at https://www.wang-lab.science. Position description The Department of Plant Pathology in the College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences at the University of California, Davis is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Plant Pathology with an emphasis on plant health and microbiomes. This is an academic year (9-month), tenure-track Assistant Professor position that includes an appointment in the California Agricultural Experiment Station (AES), with responsibility for research and outreach relevant to the AES mission, as well as university service. The appointee is expected to establish a competitive, externally funded research program in plant microbiome science that addresses critical and emerging issues in plant pathology. The program should advance microbiome-informed approaches to the diagnosis, prediction, and/or management of plant diseases and develop science-based solutions to promote plant health. Research should generate fundamental and applied understanding of the composition, function, and/or dynamics of plant-associated microbial communities (including bacteria, fungi, oomycetes, viruses, and/or other microorganisms) and their interactions with plant hosts and each other. Areas of interest may include disease-suppressive microbiomes, dysbiosis and pathobiomes, host-microbiome-pathogen interactions, pathogen-pathogen and pathogen-nonpathogen interactions, disease complexes and multi-infections, microbiome engineering, synthetic communities, and the ecology and evolution of pathogens within the phytomicrobiome. Research may also address climate-driven changes in plant-microbiome interactions and emerging diseases, span model, agricultural, and/or natural plant systems, and should have a strong mechanistic and/or predictive foundation. The appointee will complement existing departmental strengths in plant-microbe interactions, disease epidemiology, and disease management, while expanding microbiome-informed approaches relevant to food security, agricultural sustainability, climate resilience, and the broader One Health framework. The appointee will be expected to teach GDB103: The Microbiome of People, Animals and Plants, a 3-unit, upper-division undergraduate course that serves Global Disease Biology (GDB) and other students. The appointee is also expected to contribute to required GDB courses, such as GDB90: Introduction to Global Disease Biology, GDB 187: Global Disease Biology Seminar, and PMI129Y: One Health: Human, Animal & Environment Interfaces, and will have opportunities to contribute to graduate courses such as PLP201B: Ecology and Epidemiology of Plant Pathogenic Organisms and PLP298: Microbial Ecology. Training and mentoring of graduate students, undergraduate student advising, curricular development, outreach, and departmental and university service are expected. The successful candidate will be an active member of the Plant Pathology Graduate Program and other graduate groups as appropriate and will have opportunities to collaborate with Cooperative Extension specialists and advisors, relevant industries, and other public stakeholders. This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant Professor rank, and the resulting appointment will be at that rank regardless of the appointee's qualifications.

The Department of Surgery, Division of Urology at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) in Galveston, Texas is seeking three (3) Board Certified/Board Eligible Urologists to support clinical growth across the UTMB health system: (1) a General Urologist based in Galveston with participation in Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) care, (2) a General Urologist based in Angleton/Lake Jackson focused on community access and practice development, and (3) a Fellowship-trained Urologist (e.g., Endourology, Men’s Health, or Urologic Oncology) with opportunity to develop a subspecialty program while also contributing to general urology services. Pain is the most common reason people come to an ED, and treatment still depends on a small set of medications, several of which carry risk of misuse. Approaches such as mindfulness-based interventions and virtual reality have a growing evidence base in outpatient and chronic pain settings, but much less is known about whether they can be delivered during an ED visit, which patients will engage with them, and how to measure that engagement in a short and often interrupted encounter. The successful candidate will work across emergency care, pain research, behavioral intervention, and implementation science. The Department of Internal Medicine at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) stands at an exciting crossroads of growth and transformation. As we continue Moving Medicine Forward, our focus is on advancing our tripartite mission – delivering high-value care, driving research, innovation, and cultivating excellence in medical education.
Our team is redefining what it means to deliver care in an academic setting – where access efficiency, discovery, and quality outcomes go hand in hand. We are investing in people, processes, and technology to create an environment where collaboration thrives, and every role contributes to advancing medicine.
With more than 140 faculty and 46 Advanced Practice Providers – and growing – the Department of Medicine is committed to fostering excellence across all mission areas. About the Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology
The Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) is a dynamic and growing program within the Department of Medicine dedicated to excellence in patient care, research, and education. The Division includes more than 20 faculty and Advanced Practice Providers representing the full breadth of gastroenterology and hepatology specialties.
Faculty practices across four hospitals – Galveston, League City, Clear Lake, and Angleton Danbury – providing comprehensive inpatient and outpatient services, advanced endoscopic are, multidisciplinary management of complex liver disease.
Our ACGME-accredited Gastroenterology Fellowship Program trains nine fellows across three years, offering a broad and rigorous curriculum supported by committed faculty mentors and diverse clinical experiences. The Division also plays an active role in medical student and resident education, contributing to the academic mission of the institution.
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:
• Provide comprehensive outpatient and/or inpatient gastroenterology care, including management of liver disease, inflammatory bowel disease, gastrointestinal cancers, and other digestive disorders.
• Participate in endoscopic procedures, as appropriate to training and experience.
• Supervise and teach medical students, residents, and fellows in both clinical and didactic settings.
• Engage in departmental and divisional quality improvement, patient safety, and evidence-based practice initiatives.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams—including surgery, oncology, radiology, and nutrition—for optimal patient outcomes.
• Contribute to curriculum development, clinical skills training, and other academic programs.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
• MD or DO degree from an accredited medical school.
• Board certified or board eligible in Internal Medicine and Gastroenterology.
• Eligible for medical licensure in the State of Texas.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
• Experience in an academic medical center or teaching environment.
• Demonstrated involvement in scholarly activity, clinical research, quality improvement projects, or curriculum development.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills with a collaborative, team-oriented approach.

Commensurate with experience.
